title: Localize the surface, not the concept
statement: Localize a question's surface, such as names, places and everyday objects, but never its concept, its standard units or a context the lesson needs.
detail: One evaluation framework for generated questions requires 'culturally appropriate names, locations, objects, and contexts' in every question, and lists what is never localized: universal mathematical and scientific concepts, international context when pedagogically necessary, and standard units of measurement (`icloud-work/incept/incept-uae-api-website/inceptapi.com/INCEPT_Benchmarking_Framework.html`). The generator's cultural guidelines add that cultural points apply only where 'genuinely relevant to the learning objective' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/spiky_points_of_view.json`). Both are adopted rules, with no measurement.
against: The same guidelines also direct one cultural framing everywhere: 'Prioritize Arabic and Islamic perspectives in all explanations.' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/spiky_points_of_view.json`, line 9), against their own rule that cultural points apply only where relevant.

evidence.quote: Our localization framework ensures that all generated questions use culturally appropriate names, locations, objects, and contexts relevant to UAE students.
Only apply spiky points that are genuinely relevant to the learning objective
